sections_target.text: This document sets out the P1 maintenance procedures to be carried out annually, as shown above by the code Y1. The document was prepared from the documents previously prepared by the Holding Company for Electrical Power Distribution, and it was discussed, amended and approved by the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.

This maintenance is carried out to preserve the low-voltage network equipment and return it to its normal condition, provided the work is completed on the same day, so that supply continues and sudden faults are avoided.

rows: Issue a work permit (work order); the workers on site must carry an occupational safety and health category card.
Place the appropriate warning signs.
The occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment must be followed.
Make sure both sources of supply are disconnected from the line to be worked on, that there is no voltage on it, and that it is earthed from both sides.
Occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety belt, etc.
Cleaning tools for insulators, insulators, spare insulated conductors.
Tree trimming tools.
Portable earth.
A suitable set of tools and screwdrivers.
Replace damaged network components or repair them (insulators, conductors), provided they can be completed on the same day.
Check the tightening of the cables to the overhead network.
Re-compress cable ends that are not well compressed.
Make sure the low-voltage cables rising on the poles are placed in protective pipes.
Make sure the length of the low-voltage routes is not excessive and conforms to specifications (700 m for the city, 1000 m for the village), so that it does not cause voltage drop.
Make sure the sag of the conductors is appropriate.
Clean the insulators and check the spacing between them, so that it is not less than 20 cm.
Check the switches and fuses feeding the outgoing feeders (sorties) in the kiosks.
Check the service connections to houses and make sure they are sound.
Make sure the earth is properly connected to all poles, and the repeated earth.
Trim the trees interfering with the line.

Introduction
This document sets out the P1 maintenance procedures to be carried out annually, as shown above by the code Y1. The document was prepared from the documents previously prepared by the Holding Company for Electrical Power Distribution, and it was discussed, amended and approved by the MPIS coordinators of the electricity distribution companies.
This maintenance is carried out to preserve the low-voltage network equipment and return it to its normal condition, provided the work is completed on the same day, so that supply continues and sudden faults are avoided.
Safety Precautions
Issue a work permit (work order); the workers on site must carry an occupational safety and health category card. | 
Place the appropriate warning signs. | 
The occupational safety and health procedures for personnel and equipment must be followed. | 
Make sure both sources of supply are disconnected from the line to be worked on, that there is no voltage on it, and that it is earthed from both sides. | 
Tools, Instruments and Equipment Used
Occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety belt, etc. | 
Cleaning tools for insulators, insulators, spare insulated conductors. | 
Tree trimming tools. | 
Portable earth. | 
A suitable set of tools and screwdrivers. | 
Procedures to be Carried Out
Replace damaged network components or repair them (insulators, conductors), provided they can be completed on the same day. | 1.
Check the tightening of the cables to the overhead network. | 2.
Re-compress cable ends that are not well compressed. | 3.
Make sure the low-voltage cables rising on the poles are placed in protective pipes. | 4.
Make sure the length of the low-voltage routes is not excessive and conforms to specifications (700 m for the city, 1000 m for the village), so that it does not cause voltage drop. | 5.
Make sure the sag of the conductors is appropriate. | 6.
Clean the insulators and check the spacing between them, so that it is not less than 20 cm. | 7.
Check the switches and fuses feeding the outgoing feeders (sorties) in the kiosks. | 8.
Check the service connections to houses and make sure they are sound. | 9.
Make sure the earth is properly connected to all poles, and the repeated earth. | 10.
Trim the trees interfering with the line. | 11.
